text: Many different construction methods were used. Firstly, there are earth dug post holes in the corners that held up the roof. Then there are sill beams along the floor with a groove cut into which planks would have been placed to form the wall. This kind of sill beam with a groove for planks has never before been found in Nordic churches. This is interesting and important, says [Dagfinn] Skre. Stone supports for the benches were found inside the walls. Skre thinks that the chancel was a bit higher than the stone floor of the church nave, and observes that it was covered with a wooden floor planks. Remnants of turf walls were found outside the church. It is remarkable to see how the planks were inserted in the sill beams. This is very uncommon, says [Jesse] Byock. The sill beams were still intact says Byock and now they will be dried. The timber was very well-preserved and that means that oxygen did not come into contact with it. When asked whether he found any items inside the church, Byock says, there was very little, except for small pieces of copper and iron. Under the church there seems to be the remnants of an earlier farm building. Byock says that it seems that fire had broken out in the church and that the wood is in some places scorched, but we dont have any sources about the burning of the church. Skre thinks there is reason to reconstruct the church at Hrísbrú, and thereby giving people the possibility to travel back in time. This is one of the very few cases where we have a great deal of information about what the construction type was and how it was built. Therefore, it is very easy to make a good replica. He says that he hopes that authorities will start such a reconstruction. He says that this would be a nice contribution to the people of the Mosfell Valley concerning life there in the past. Morgunblaðið, 5th of August, 2004
